title: SharePoint: Remove-SPOFontFile cmdlet to delete brand font files
summary: The deletion commands, multi-geo restrictions and fallback behaviour are supported. The checklist nevertheless directs administrators to look for font packages in the Brand Fonts library, a location Microsoft does not document for packages; the licensing field also understates the published SharePoint licence requirement.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing
claims.claim: SharePoint is introducing Remove-SPOFontFile to delete brand font files from the Brand Fonts library used by the brand center.
claims.quote: Microsoft SharePoint is introducing PowerShell support for deleting brand font files from the Brand Fonts library used by the SharePoint Brand Center.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: SharePoint administrators can remove brand font files that are no longer approved, licensed or needed.
claims.quote: With the new Remove-SPOFontFile cmdlet, SharePoint administrators can remove brand font files that are no longer approved, licensed, or needed across their organization in SharePoint.

claims.where: controls[0].api; What's changing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Remove-SPOFontFile -Name <font file name> is the documented deletion call in Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Module: Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell Module
Remove-SPOFontFile -Name "Tahoma.ttf"
This example removes the SharePoint brand font file "Tahoma.ttf" from the brand fonts library across all geo locations.

claims.where: summary; controls[0]; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Removing a font file deletes it from the tenant's primary geo and all satellite geos.
claims.quote: The font file is deleted from the primary geo and all satellite geos.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: After removal the font file is no longer available for use in SharePoint.
claims.quote: After removal, the font file will no longer be available for use in SharePoint.

claims.quote: Attempting to remove a font file from a satellite geo will result in a warning.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Custom brand fonts are managed in the brand center's Brand Fonts library, whose documentation points to Remove-SPOFontFile.
claims.quote:
To manage your custom brand fonts, you'll need to navigate to the Brand Fonts library in the Brand center app.
To remove a custom font file from the tenant's brand fonts library across all geo locations, use Remove-SPOFontFile.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: SharePoint brand center app > Brand Fonts library > font file > Visible reaches the font availability property.
claims.quote:
To manage your custom brand fonts, you'll need to navigate to the Brand Fonts library in the Brand center app.
1. Select your custom font file from the library.
2. Edit the Visible property on your font file to control the availability of the font for experiences.

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Editing Visible controls font availability for experiences without removing the font file.
claims.quote:
Edit the Visible property on your font file to control the availability of the font for experiences.
To remove a custom font file from the tenant's brand fonts library across all geo locations, use Remove-SPOFontFile.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document an admin UI operation to delete a custom brand font file.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand fonts delete font file brand center app UI removal. Opened Brand Fonts and Remove-SPOFontFile; the former documents Visible and directs removal to PowerShell, with no UI deletion procedure.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls
claims.claim: No automation for setting a custom font file's Visible property is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand font file Visible property set PowerShell REST API. Read Brand Fonts and results for Set-SPOFontPackage and Set-SPOBuiltInFontPackageSettings; those act on packages, not a custom font file's Visible property.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Remove-SPOFontPackage -Identity <font package GUID> removes a custom font package from the tenant.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet removes a custom font package from the tenant.
Remove-SPOFontPackage -Identity 12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789012
This example removes the font package with the specified GUID.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Removing a font package does not delete its associated brand font files.
claims.quote: Removing a font package does not delete the associated brand font files.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls
claims.claim: A UI procedure to delete a font package is not documented, and packages cannot be deleted from the brand center app.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand center delete font package app UI. Opened Font packages and Remove-SPOFontPackage. Font packages states: 'Font packages cannot be deleted from the brand center app'; removal is documented through PowerShell.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Font packages can be edited or made not visible in the brand center app.
claims.quote: Font packages cannot be deleted from the brand center app, they can be edited or made not visible to remove from selection experiences.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the cmdlet's default availability or any automatic deletion behaviour on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Remove-SPOFontFile rollout default enabled automatic. Read the roadmap record, Remove-SPOFontFile and Brand Fonts. They describe introducing and invoking the cmdlet, not its default availability or automatic execution.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licence model is unknown because no licence specific to the deletion cmdlet is published.
claims.quote: To access SharePoint, users in your organization need to be assigned a license that includes SharePoint.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the explanation of the unknown model with: 'SharePoint's service description says users accessing SharePoint need an assigned licence that includes SharePoint. No licence specific to Remove-SPOFontFile is published at the time of writing (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/sharepoint-online-service-description/sharepoint-online-service-description and retain the separate font-licence requirement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cmdlet, Brand Fonts and brand center overview pages name no product licence specific to deleting a brand font file.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand center Remove-SPOFontFile licensing SharePoint Online subscription requirements. Opened Remove-SPOFontFile, Brand Fonts, brand center overview and SharePoint service description; no deletion-specific licence was stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no meter for the brand font deletion operation in the cited documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint brand fonts removal price meter billing. Opened Remove-SPOFontFile, Brand Fonts and brand center overview; read billing search results concerning Embedded and document processing, not brand font deletion.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Any font used in Microsoft 365 applications requires a font licence covering the intended use.
claims.quote: Any font used in Microsoft 365 applications requires a font license that covers the conditions of font usage for the intended product.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: For fonts Microsoft did not supply, the organisation must review the accompanying licence agreements.
claims.quote: For fonts obtained elsewhere or supplied with other apps, you'll need to review the license agreements that accompany those applications.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Publishing brand fonts creates font catalog files stored publicly in the cloud alongside the fonts.
claims.quote: By using this feature and publishing font files, a font catalog is created. The newly created font catalog files are publicly stored, along with the fonts, in the cloud

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The published files are accessible to anyone, including outsiders, who obtains their URLs.
claims.quote: The files are accessible to anyone, even people outside of your organization, who can get the URLs that link to them.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft advises against using the feature with fonts whose licences restrict cloud hosting.
claims.quote: Don't use this feature if your fonts contain proprietary information, or if they have license usage restrictions, such as restrictions on cloud hosting

claims.quote: Brand fonts require Public CDN because SharePoint uses it to host font files.

claims.quote: If Public CDN isn't enabled, a Global Administrator must enable it before brand managers can add fonts.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, second bullet
claims.claim: Get-SPOFontPackage can be used to inspect the tenant's custom font packages.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet retrieves one or more custom font packages in the tenant.
Get-SPOFontPackage

claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/get-spofontpackage?view=sharepoint-ps to sources for the existing Get-SPOFontPackage recommendation.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, second bullet
claims.claim: Administrators can find font packages, as well as font files, in the Brand Fonts library.
claims.quote: Searched: "font packages" "Brand Fonts library" stored. Read Brand Fonts, Font packages and Get-SPOFontPackage; the library contains uploaded font files, but no passage directs readers there to find package records.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'Identify font files in the Brand Fonts library that are no longer approved, using the brand center app, and inspect custom font packages with Get-SPOFontPackage.' The documented file location is https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/brand-fonts and the package command is https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.online.sharepoint.powershell/get-spofontpackage?view=sharepoint-ps.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet; Governance controls

claims.quote: Checklist: 'check whether Public CDN was enabled when the brand center was set up'. Table rows govern deleting a font file, a font file's Visible property, and removing a font package; none governs Public CDN.
claims.fix: Remove the parenthetical Public CDN path and the instruction to check that setting from the first Before rollout bullet. Replace that bullet with: 'Confirm with brand managers whether custom brand fonts are in use.' Do not add a control row.
